The crux is whether a logician applies the formal logical definition (X → Y) or the counterfactual/causal definition of "sufficient cause." Candidate A correctly identifies both frameworks and explains that when discussing causes (not mere conditions), the counterfactual interpretation governs: X must be such that Y depends on it. Since crystals form regardless of Reagent X, it fails this test. Candidates C, D, and G argue YES using only the formal definition (X → Y holds) without recognizing that "cause" invokes causal reasoning, which requires the counterfactual. Candidates B, E, and F correctly conclude NO but with less sophisticated framing. A edges ahead by showing the distinction a logician would make explicit.
</why>
